oracle.scope: One iCloud Mail app-specific password from signed local capture through device-only macOS Keychain storage, opaque-reference configuration, read-only production authentication, daemon observation, replacement, recovery, restore, and removal.
oracle.invariant: Only the accepted signed user-context principals can administer or resolve the credential; no supported boundary transports or persists the raw secret outside the broker input, Keychain, and the bounded in-process authentication copy required by ImapFlow.
oracle.precedence: This oracle owns the V1 mailbox-credential, local-administration, lifecycle, recovery, onboarding primitive, and evidence-tier authority. The issue 203 oracle remains action-approval authority, issue 213 remains numeric CLI-exit authority, and the existing sync statechart remains the runtime credential-generation authority. None is widened into another capability.
oracle.compatibilityRule: Changing a provider endpoint, password method, signed principal, access group, Keychain attribute, local operation, secret boundary, state transition, generation gate, recovery ordering, removal meaning, or evidence claim requires a new oracle digest and renewed security review.
oracle.digestConvention: The normative SHA-256 is the hash of this file's exact UTF-8 bytes. The checked views and checker pin that raw-byte digest; this file does not contain a self-referential digest field.

executionProfile.failureDomain: the five icloud-credential-authority v1 artifacts only

productBoundary.futureAuthorization: Apple Account direct third-party authorization remains future research. Current Apple support pages describe supported apps but expose no public Agent Mail enrollment or protocol authority; V1 does not claim or wait for it.

providerInterface.futureMethodRule: A future Apple authorization method requires a new discriminant, oracle digest, secret and token authority, enrollment proof, migration state, and qualification. It cannot be selected as fallback from this method.

usernameCandidates.when: initial candidate; retain it for transient retries until a structural authentication rejection
only after a structural authentication rejection of local-part for the same generation and only when the shared three-session budget has capacity

attemptBudget.scope: one credential generation across both username candidates
attemptBudget.sessionAccounting: Every DNS/TCP/TLS/IMAP session start consumes one of three total attempts; there is no nested or per-candidate budget.
attemptBudget.structuralRejection: A structural local-part authentication rejection advances immediately to full-address without a delay; a structural full-address rejection enters authentication-blocked and starts no retry.
attemptBudget.transientFailure: Retry the current candidate after the delay indexed by the just-consumed attempt when another total attempt remains. Exhaustion returns account.provider_unavailable and never authentication-blocked.

schedules.outcome: account.provider_unavailable because no session remains for full-address

noFallbacks: OAuth or Apple Account authorization without a new accepted authority
environment, file, stdin, argv, or test-client credential injection

platform.reason: macOS 12 is the first release with xpc_connection_set_peer_code_signing_requirement for C XPC. No PID-only, audit-token-only, undocumented, or unauthenticated compatibility path exists.
platform.userContext: logged-in GUI user bootstrap and audit session
platform.distribution: versioned checksummed and notarized Homebrew Cask containing the intact signed app bundle

owns the LocalAccountAuthorityActor, nonsecret journal/config writes, one-shot validator launch, and user LaunchAgent registration
shows the native secure field and performs exact-reference SecItem add, existence check, and delete

launchAgents.label: dev.johnlombardo.agent-mail.credential-broker
launchAgents.registration: user bootstrap before the credential ceremony; on-demand only

launchAgents.label: dev.johnlombardo.agent-mail.daemon
launchAgents.registration: installed and started only after authentication, discovery, active-config promotion, and production one-shot validation succeed

bundleTopology.oneShotValidation: The nested CLI verifies and spawns PRINCIPAL-DAEMON's exact installed executable with only --credential-validation-worker in argv. An inherited anonymous C XPC endpoint begins with the daemon's non-authority random challenge and completes the same symmetric authenticated hello as broker XPC before any factory input is encoded. The credentialRef never enters argv or environment.

signing.profiles: separate Developer ID distribution provisioning profiles embedded in CLI, broker, and daemon app-like nested bundles; the outer container has no Keychain group
releaseInputs: CLI, broker, and daemon provisioning profile UUIDs and expiry
nested CLI, broker, and daemon cdhashes
notarization ticket and Cask artifact SHA-256
signing.acceptedRequirementTemplate: anchor apple generic and identifier "<BUNDLE_ID>" and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "<APPLE_TEAM_ID>"
signing.exactReleaseManifest: After every nested principal is signed, the build inspects those immutable signed outputs and writes one canonical credential-principals.v1.json containing only nested CLI, broker, and daemon identities, requirements, cdhashes, profile facts, access groups, and entitlement digests. The outer signature is applied later and seals that manifest plus all nested code. The manifest never contains the outer cdhash, outer artifact hash, or notarization ticket.

construction.effect: compile the immutable unsigned outer container and three nested app-like bundles
sign nested PRINCIPAL-CLI and freeze its code bytes
sign nested PRINCIPAL-BROKER and freeze its code bytes
sign nested PRINCIPAL-DAEMON and freeze its code bytes
inspect signed nested outputs and generate canonical credential-principals.v1.json without any outer-signature-derived value
sign the outer bundle last so its resource seal covers the final manifest and nested bundles
notarize and staple without mutating sealed resources
compute detached release-record and Cask artifact SHA-256 outside the signed bundle

signing.acyclicityInvariant: No SBUILD step reads its own output or a later output. Nested cdhashes exist before manifest generation; manifest bytes exist before outer signing; outer cdhash and artifact hash exist only after the manifest is sealed and remain detached.
signing.signedInstalledConstructionProof: Qualification must build in SBUILD order, verify codesign --verify --deep --strict and spctl on the installed outer bundle, parse each embedded profile and entitlement, recompute every nested requirement/cdhash/entitlements digest against the sealed manifest, verify the outer resource seal, and show that changing the manifest or any nested byte makes strict verification fail. Design evidence does not claim this proof has run.
signing.resignedDefinition: Any ad-hoc, unsigned, wrong-team, wrong-identifier, invalid-profile, invalid-seal, or cdhash-not-in-the-installed-manifest copy is re-signed and denied. A future legitimate release is accepted only through its separately signed replacement manifest and installed upgrade transaction.

keychainAuthority.implementation: Security.framework SecItem API with kSecUseDataProtectionKeychain=true on every add, query, and delete

item.kSecAttrDescription: Dedicated Apple app-specific password for Agent Mail
item.kSecAttrGeneric: canonical UTF-8 metadata: schemaVersion, installationId, providerId, credentialRevision, transactionId, referenceSha256, createdAt; never email or password

reference.binding: the reference, installationId, providerId, revision, transactionId, and referenceSha256 must agree between config/journal and kSecAttrGeneric

passwordInput.reason: Apple does not publish a stable app-password presentation format; the broker preserves the entered value without guessing or silently rewriting it.

keychainAuthority.duplicatePolicy: SecItemAdd only. Never update a secret in place. Exact class+service+account+group duplicate is idempotent only when metadata matches the durable transaction; any other duplicate is duplicateCredential and blocks repair.
keychainAuthority.replacementPolicy: Create a new reference and revision, validate it, atomically promote nonsecret configuration, start/observe the daemon, then delete the old exact reference. The old item remains authoritative until promotion and is never overwritten.
keychainAuthority.enumerationPolicy: Never enumerate or adopt arbitrary service items. Recovery may query only the exact active, old, or pending references named by validated owner-only configuration or journal state.
keychainAuthority.firstUnlock: Before the first user unlock after restart, resolution returns keychainBeforeFirstUnlock and the daemon exposes a stable nonhealthy state with no timer and no retry. After a trusted first-unlock observation, the same revision may retry; screen lock after first unlock does not make this accessibility class unavailable.
keychainAuthority.differentDevice: ThisDeviceOnly items do not migrate. A different-device or empty-target restore necessarily enters credentialsRequired.
keychainAuthority.threatLimit: Keychain access groups trust profile-authorized code from the release signing team. Compromise of the Developer ID identity or authorized provisioning profile is not mitigated by an additional local cdhash check and requires certificate/profile response plus credential replacement.

localAdministration.transport: C XPC Mach service in the logged-in user's bootstrap namespace

authenticatedHello.challengeAuthority: none; the first frame discloses only protocol constants, a random handshake identifier and challenge, and a monotonic expiry

bindings.challengeBinding: SHA-256 of canonical UTF-8 domain agent-mail-peer-v1/client, protocolVersion, handshakeId bytes, serverChallenge bytes, clientNonce bytes, initiator principal id, and acceptor principal id
bindings.clientBinding: SHA-256 of canonical UTF-8 domain agent-mail-peer-v1/server, protocolVersion, handshakeId bytes, serverChallenge bytes, clientNonce bytes, initiator principal id, and acceptor principal id

verificationOrder: set the exact role-specific peer code-signing requirement on the connection before activation
acceptor emits one memory-only single-use ServerChallengeV1 before decoding any peer-provided operation metadata or opening UI
initiator derives SecCode and audit-token facts from the received challenge message, verifies requirement, sealed-manifest cdhash, effective UID, and audit session, then sends ClientHelloV1

acceptor derives SecCode and audit-token facts from the received hello message, verifies requirement, sealed-manifest cdhash, effective UID, audit session, challenge binding, expiry, and single-use state, then sends ServerAcceptedV1

initiator derives SecCode and audit-token facts from the received accepted message, repeats requirement, sealed-manifest cdhash, effective UID, and audit-session checks, verifies the client binding, then and only then may encode an operation request
authenticatedHello.wrongPeerPostcondition: Any wrong requirement, cdhash, effective UID, audit session, malformed frame, wrong binding, expired challenge, or replay closes the connection with zero operation decoding, zero operation metadata disclosure, zero UI, zero Keychain/config/journal/service/provider effect, and only a bounded aggregate denial counter.
authenticatedHello.receiptBinding: The operation envelope binds transcriptSha256 for this connection, but canonical idempotency digest and durable receipt exclude the ephemeral handshake so a legitimate retry through a new authenticated handshake returns the same receipt.

preparse: complete authenticatedHello before operation metadata exists
derive SecCode and audit-token facts from every received hello, acceptance, request, and response message
verify exact role-specific requirement, sealed-manifest cdhash, effective UID, and audit-session identity on every received frame
callerAuthentication.reverseAuthentication: The CLI authenticates broker or validator from the received challenge and acceptance messages before sending operation metadata; acceptors authenticate the CLI from the received hello and request messages before decoding operation payloads.
callerAuthentication.failure: drop before operation decoding or UI; record only a bounded safe denial counter

authorization.credential.store: only a durable CLI transaction naming a new exact reference, revision, account display identity, and Apple label; the password is collected inside the broker UI
authorization.credential.exists: only an exact reference named by validated active, pending, old, or removal-journal authority
authorization.credential.remove: only an exact reference named by validated active, pending, old, or removal-journal authority and a journaled compensation, generation-healthy replacement cleanup, or user-confirmed account removal

receiptLedger.canonicalDigest: SHA-256 of canonical version, operation, requestId, requestNonce, and payload; excludes ephemeral handshakeId and transcriptSha256
admissionOrder: fail closed on corrupt receipt data or a wall clock earlier than the journal high-water mark
compact every receipt whose expiresAt is less than or equal to now and fsync the compacted journal
return the existing receipt when identity and canonical digest match, even when 256 records remain
return account.request_replayed when the identity matches and canonical digest differs
when 256 unexpired unique receipts remain, reject the next unique mutation as account.receipt_capacity before UI or any effect
otherwise reserve and fsync the unique mutation receipt before UI or another effect

capacityError.retryAfter: ceiling seconds until the earliest unexpired receipt expires; minimum 1
capacityError.postcondition: The rejected 257th unique request creates no receipt and causes zero UI, Keychain, config, service, validator, provider, or network effect.

receiptLedger.statusAccounting: account.status is nonmutating, consumes no receipt slot, and reads the last validated snapshot.
receiptLedger.clockRule: Persist maxObservedWallClock. A backward clock or corrupt expiry fails closed as account.internal before compaction or effect; no attacker-controlled expiry is accepted.

localAdministration.replay: Under the receipt-ledger admission order, an identical mutation returns the same safe receipt, changed content under the same request identity is replay, and the 257th unique unexpired mutation is rejected before UI/effect.
localAdministration.concurrency: One mutation actor owns the journal lock. A second mutation returns account.operation_busy without opening UI or touching Keychain. Status consumes the last validated snapshot.
localAdministration.disconnect: Cancellation is requested, then the owner awaits the active child and idempotent compensation. A process kill leaves a durable recoverable step; rerun, not an unjournaled best effort, converges it.
localAdministration.clipboard: The broker supports the platform's ordinary Paste action directly into NSSecureTextField. It never reads, records, synchronizes, or silently clears the general pasteboard and does not claim control over prior clipboard synchronization or unrelated clipboard readers. The UI tells the user to clear the source clipboard if their password manager did not do so.
localAdministration.publicReachability: No HTTP route, bearer scope, OpenAPI path, daemon public-operation entry, Tailscale surface, or demo operation may dispatch a local credential operation or open broker UI.

secretAuthority.rawSecretDefinition: The Apple app-specific password in text or bytes, including encoded, quoted, interpolated, serialized, exception, or diagnostic forms.

permittedLocations.location: NSSecureTextField and a bounded mutable native Data buffer
permittedLocations.cleanup: clear field, overwrite mutable Data, release UI, and exit the broker after the transaction

permittedLocations.location: kSecValueData in the exact data-protection Keychain item
permittedLocations.cleanup: exact-reference SecItemDelete only during compensation, generation-healthy replacement cleanup, or confirmed account removal

permittedLocations.location: bounded daemon Keychain CFData/mutable Data plus ImapFlow auth.pass string during one connection authentication
permittedLocations.cleanup: zero mutable buffers; immediately after connect settles assign empty auth.pass, delete auth.pass, close on failure, drop client references; set RLIMIT_CORE=0

secretAuthority.deterministicZeroizationLimit: ImapFlow requires a JavaScript string, so garbage-collected immutable copies cannot be proven deterministically zeroized. The design minimizes lifetime, disables core dumps and logs, exits the one-shot validator, and keeps this limitation in security qualification.

removalTransactionSchema.firstEffectRule: The complete record is atomically written, file-fsynced, renamed, and parent-fsynced before stop/unload, plist unlink, Keychain delete, binding unlink, or any other removal effect.

configurationAuthority.restoreRule: Restore the safe projection, mark its reference unverified, query only that exact reference in the installed user context, and enter credentialsRequired when it is absent, inaccessible, metadata-mismatched, from another installation, or from another device.

stateMachine.cancellation: the owner alone accepts cancellation, propagates it to the broker/validator/service child, and awaits one idempotent cleanup before a terminal receipt

transitions.effect: persist the failed removal phase, cursor, exact target set, and safe classified error

transitions.effect: advance once to full-address without delay and without resetting the three-session budget
transitions.postcondition: the next provider session, if any, uses full-address under the same credential revision and shared attempt count

runtimeGenerationGate.releaseRule: Only a strictly newer accepted candidate revision can leave authentication-blocked. Equal, older, process restart, timer, network recovery, screen unlock, daemon restart, config rewrite without a new accepted item, or repeated provider output cannot release it.
runtimeGenerationGate.staleFailureRule: An authentication failure from an older bound attempt cleans up and restarts only the latest revision; it cannot block or overwrite the newer revision.
runtimeGenerationGate.retryRule: authentication-blocked owns zero actors, sockets, and retry timers

connectionFactory.name: createProductionIcloudConnectionV1

clientHandle.const: internal connected ImapFlow 1.7.1 handle with bounded cleanup ownership

connectionFactory.resolution: Validate config and Keychain metadata binding in the daemon process, then pass the transient password only to the pinned ImapFlow constructor.
connectionFactory.validationSequence: Instantiate a validation-only ImapFlow subclass whose run method rejects commands outside the exact allowlist before dispatch. Call connect() with verifyOnly=false and includeMailboxes=false, call listIcloudMailboxesReadOnly(client) exactly once after authentication, retain only normalized rows, then logout and close. The owned adapter constructively supplies listOnly:true; no general sync client or caller may choose or widen these options.

listOnlyAuthority.installedBehavior: In ImapFlow 1.7.1 lib/commands/list.js, listOnly makes canRequestSubscribed false and returns after the primary LIST or XLIST result, before INBOX fixup, LSUB, and STATUS queries.

typeAuthority.observedDeclaration: Installed ImapFlow 1.7.1 exports ListOptions without listOnly and declares ImapFlow.list(options?: ListOptions): Promise<ListResponse[]>.
typeAuthority.compiler: installed Vite+ 0.2.9 vp lint --type-aware --type-check against the repository node_modules and an exact strict noEmit Bundler-resolution tsconfig
typeAuthority.constructiveInvariant: The exported function accepts only Pick<ImapFlow, "list">, constructs a typed IcloudListOnlyOptions variable with literal true, and passes that variable to a private forwardListOnly adapter accepting exactly ListOptions & { readonly listOnly: true }. There is no direct excess-property object-literal call and no escape hatch.

listOnlyAuthority.runtimeTranscript: Against the exact IMAPFLOW-LIST hash, invoke the installed list command with the adapter's constructively typed {listOnly:true} options for all five capability branches. Each branch must emit exactly one LIST or XLIST matching this table, with no RETURN token, LSUB, or STATUS; this isolated transcript is design/dependency evidence, not production or live evidence.

connectionFactory.mailboxResult: Pass only the listIcloudMailboxesReadOnly(client) LIST or XLIST result through the pinned adapter into normalizeMailboxList. The adapter alone constructs ListOptions & { readonly listOnly: true }; no mailbox is selected or examined and no body, flags, subscription state, or message data are fetched.
connectionFactory.commandGuard: The validation-only subclass rejects every command before dispatch unless it is CAPABILITY, ID, LOGIN, AUTHENTICATE, NAMESPACE, LIST, XLIST, or LOGOUT. Installed-version probes lock each capability branch and assert LSUB, STATUS, RETURN(SUBSCRIBED), mailbox-open, fetch, and mutation commands remain absent.

transientRetry.budgetScope: shared across local-part and full-address for one credential generation

errorCategories.source: authenticated plus normalized LIST and logout
structural ImapFlow authenticationFailed or accepted server response code
errorCategories.outcome: local-part advances once to full-address when the shared budget has capacity, local-part exhaustion is provider-unavailable, and full-address is authentication-blocked

errorCategories.source: data-protection Keychain unavailable before first unlock
certificate, hostname, trust, or TLS-version failure
unexpected provider/ImapFlow result or mailbox list
metadata, generation, cleanup, or implementation invariant failure

connectionFactory.logging: No ImapFlow logger, raw logs, log events, password-bearing URL, provider exception text, nested cause, or raw response crosses the adapter. Only fixed category, accountId, revision, attempt count, and correlationId are retained.
connectionFactory.lifetime: A validation worker exits after logout and cleanup. A sync client deletes auth.pass immediately after connect settles and resolves it afresh only for a later connection; it never retains a reconnect password source.

operationAuthority.sharedValidation: one contracts-owned Zod model parsed from unknown for both guided and structured local paths
operationAuthority.sharedOutcome: issue 213/214 command-outcome and output-context adapters select existing semantic kinds and exits; command handlers contain no numeric policy

details.oneOfFrom: operationAuthority.errors exact details schema selected by code

errors.fixedMessage: A signed local user interaction is required.
iCloud authentication is blocked until credentials are replaced.
The Keychain is unavailable until this user unlocks the Mac.
The local credential authority denied this caller.
The iCloud Mail authentication protocol failed safely.
Another local account operation is active.
The local account request was rejected as a replay.
The local request receipt capacity is temporarily full.
The configured credential reference is stale.
The local account operation was cancelled.

operationAuthority.setupOrchestration: agent-mail setup invokes account.status then account.connect or account.repair, applies the fixed safe defaults, and waits for AccountUsableResultV1. It owns no credential capture, Keychain, validation, config, or service path of its own.
operationAuthority.guidedStructuredParity: Human and --json modes submit the same request and receive the same typed result/error before presentation. Both may launch the same native ceremony in a GUI user session. Without a GUI or when unattended input is requested, they return account.interaction_required; no plaintext noninteractive substitute exists.

removalRestoreAuthority.daemonUninstall: Stops and unregisters only dev.johnlombardo.agent-mail.daemon and removes only its exact owned plist. It preserves private archive, config, Keychain items, and Apple credentials.

removalRestoreAuthority.archiveRemoval: A separate future destructive operation with exact ownership proof; never implied by daemon uninstall or account.remove.
removalRestoreAuthority.appleRevocation: Manual at account.apple.com. Agent Mail never automates sign-in or claims server revocation from local deletion. The status remains not-performed until independent user confirmation is explicitly recorded; V1 stores no Apple session.
removalRestoreAuthority.sameDeviceReinstall: Reuse is allowed only when owner-only config/journal survives, the exact ref and metadata bind, the Keychain item is present in the same user context, and the installed signed principals carry the same access group. No scan/adoption occurs when config is lost.
removalRestoreAuthority.upgrade: A new signed release must prove the same access-group entitlement and migrate nonsecret schema transactionally before using the existing ref; wrong team/prefix/profile fails closed.
removalRestoreAuthority.emptyOrDifferentDeviceRestore: Restore safe metadata and archive, then enter credentials-required until a newly generated dedicated password is provisioned as a strictly newer revision.

requirements.text: An acyclic inside-out signed bundle and challenge-first symmetric message authentication ensure only exact signed local principals in the logged-in user context can create, query, resolve, replace, or remove the credential.
No supported interface transports or persists the raw secret outside the broker input, Keychain, and bounded daemon authentication memory.

Every partial Keychain/config/service/removal ordering, receipt admission, and retry converges through one journaled owner without silent orphan, lost cleanup reference, stale authority, duplicate install, or fallback.
Final full-address rejection after the frozen candidate sequence reaches stable authentication-blocked, and only a strictly newer accepted credential revision can release it.

Validation uses an owned no-cast adapter that constructively provides exact listOnly:true against pinned declarations and runtime capability branches, shares three total sessions across username candidates, opens no mailbox, fetches no body, and dispatches no mutation command.
Backups contain only safe explanatory metadata; restore without the exact same-device item requires reprovisioning.
Daemon uninstall, account/local-item removal, archive deletion, and Apple-side revocation remain distinct observable outcomes.
Guided setup and structured local commands share one exact request, result, error, state, semantic, exit, actor/journal, and generated-view authority.
Design, local, signed-installed, live, deployed, security, documentation, and delivery evidence remain separate.
Demo cannot import, inspect, invoke, or fall through to production credential, root, service, or network authority.

planningShieldApplicability.reason: Live issues, accepted authorities, HEAD, Apple pages, dependency version, and source hashes are pinned.
Broker, XPC, Keychain, config, validator, provider, service, backup, restore, public, demo, and human seams are mapped.
Secret, opaque reference, revision, state, result, and evidence values are traced across each transformation.
Production validation is an external IMAP effect with a strict read-only allowlist and mutation denylist.
The setup/replacement/removal protocol is an explicit persisted state machine.
Backup, restore, reinstall, removal, and Apple revocation semantics are explicit.
Guided/structured, fake/installed/live, and demo/live parity matrices are required.
Production-shaped fakes cannot substitute for signed Keychain or live Apple evidence.
Frame, receipt, transaction, authentication-attempt, timeout, and retry bounds are exact.
Signed principal, access-group, secret-sink, public/local, and provider trust boundaries dominate this design.
One secure paste, inferred settings/defaults, stable recovery, and structured outcomes remove avoidable user work.
Every evidence tier and live/deployed/security gap is labeled separately.

decisions.decision: Use one dedicated Apple app-specific password for V1 and never the primary Apple Account password.
decisions.reason: Apple documents the path for manual iCloud IMAP clients and provides individual revocation.

decisions.decision: Infer one fixed TLS IMAP provider definition and a two-candidate username rule.
decisions.reason: Apple publishes the endpoint and fallback username form; setup need not ask protocol questions.

decisions.decision: Ship an intact notarized Homebrew Cask whose separately signed nested CLI, broker, and daemon precede manifest generation and whose outer bundle is signed last.
decisions.reason: The inside-out graph makes every manifest cdhash available before the outer seal and removes any self-reference while preserving profile-authorized app-like principals.

decisions.decision: Use the data-protection Keychain, AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly, non-synchronizing, in the logged-in user context.
decisions.reason: It permits unattended background reconnect after first unlock, denies pre-unlock access, and prevents cross-device migration.

decisions.decision: Give only broker and daemon the exact Keychain access group; CLI invokes the broker and stores only nonsecret authority.
decisions.reason: The native broker captures/administers while the daemon must resolve for unattended authentication; ordinary CLI and HTTP do not need direct Keychain access.

decisions.decision: Use challenge-first C XPC with symmetric per-message SecCode, exact requirement/cdhash, UID, audit-session, nonce-binding, expiry, and replay checks; require macOS 12+.
decisions.reason: A wrong peer learns only a random non-authority challenge and cannot cause operation decoding or UI, while both initiator and acceptor authenticate the actual received message.

decisions.decision: Generate an opaque random reference and bind it to installation, provider, revision, transaction, and metadata.
decisions.reason: Configuration can explain and recover exact authority without storing or discovering a secret.

decisions.decision: Make create/replace add-only and promote a new ref before exact-deleting the old ref.
decisions.reason: In-place update would collapse generation, rollback, and crash authority.

decisions.decision: Persist one nonsecret transaction before Keychain add and recover every boundary through one LocalAccountAuthorityActor.
decisions.reason: A durable exact ref prevents silent orphan/adoption and keeps cancellation/cleanup owned.

decisions.decision: Use the signed daemon binary in one-shot mode for production validation before registering the long-running LaunchAgent.
decisions.reason: The same Keychain resolver and ImapFlow factory are exercised without starting an unvalidated service or adding another credential principal.

decisions.decision: Pin ImapFlow 1.7.1 declarations and runtime; route discovery through the owned no-cast listIcloudMailboxesReadOnly adapter, which constructs ListOptions & { readonly listOnly: true }, behind a pre-dispatch command guard and capability-branch probes.
decisions.reason: The installed declarations omit listOnly, so the constructive intersection adapter makes literal true type-check without an excess-property call or escape hatch; the pinned runtime then returns before LSUB and STATUS while preserving one bounded LIST-or-XLIST result.

decisions.decision: Treat final full-address authentication rejection, local-part candidate rejection, missing item, first unlock, network, TLS, malformed provider, and internal failure as distinct safe categories.
decisions.reason: Only a final full-address rejection should enter the stable generation-gated blocked state.

decisions.decision: Only a strictly newer accepted revision can release authentication-blocked; no retry timer exists there.
decisions.reason: The current sync statechart already models this invariant and it prevents provider retry storms.

decisions.decision: Keep account operations in a strict local registry absent from HTTP, bearer, OpenAPI, and demo surfaces.
decisions.reason: Credential administration is machine-local user authority, not remote API authority.

decisions.decision: Use one typed local operation/outcome model for guided and structured paths; setup only orchestrates it.
decisions.reason: Agents receive stable semantics without a second credential implementation or plaintext unattended shortcut.

decisions.decision: Back up only nonsecret explanatory metadata and require reprovisioning after empty/different-device restore.
decisions.reason: ThisDeviceOnly credentials do not migrate and secret export would defeat the Keychain boundary.

decisions.decision: Journal complete removal targets before the first effect, confirm each exact item absent before removing its binding, and separate uninstall, archive deletion, and manual Apple revocation.
decisions.reason: Every crash can resume from finite authority and absent cannot hide a failed Keychain cleanup or imply server revocation.

decisions.decision: Make demo isolation structural and retain eight separate evidence tiers.
decisions.reason: Credential-free evaluation and honest release claims both require absence proofs, not mode flags or broad green suites.

decisions.decision: Share three total provider sessions and two delays across both username candidates for one credential generation.
decisions.reason: A candidate fallback must not reset the retry budget or turn a transient outage into an unbounded setup loop.

decisions.decision: Retain at most 256 unexpired mutation receipts for 24 hours, compact before admission, and reject unique request 257 before UI/effect.
